subject: [PATCH] mm/zswap: fix double decrement of the LRU node count on writeback

reviews.author: Yosry Ahmed
reviews.summary: Reviewer Yosry Ahmed agrees with the original patch author's conclusion to move accounting into the isolation callback, citing concerns about noise in the code and suggesting that this change would be better than pushing more data into the callback.
reviews.raw_body:
I actually had the same thought initially, why is the walker updating
the counts? Then I reached the same conclusion that it would be too
noisy :)

I didn't look closely at the code but I agree in principle that it's
better if the callback is responsible for updating the count.

2026-10-28.patch_summary: This patch fixes a double decrement of the LRU node count on writeback in the zswap module by moving the accounting into the isolation callback, which simplifies the code and makes it more consistent with the normal list manipulation API. The change involves modifying several functions to use the __list_lru_del() function instead of the original list_lru_isolate() function. This patch addresses a long-standing issue that has been reported as noisy and may require additional backportable fixes before being fully integrated.

reviews.author: Kaitao Cheng
reviews.summary: Reviewer Kaitao Cheng evaluated three approaches to fix the double decrement of LRU node count on writeback in zswap. They initially considered pushing the accounting into the isolation callback, but deemed it too invasive and unlikely to be accepted. Next, they explored adding a new flag to enum lru_status to handle cases like zswap where the callback has already decremented the count, but decided against it due to its limited impact on the code. Finally, they implemented the patch provided in this comment, which fixes the accounting issue within zswap without requiring extensive changes across multiple subsystems.
reviews.raw_body:
I tried three approaches.

The first was "pushing the accounting into the isolation callback", as
Johannes Weiner suggested. However, as Johannes's example below also shows,
this would require extensive changes across multiple subsystems. I doubted
that such a broad change would be accepted, so I dropped this approach.

The second was to add a new flag to enum lru_status, as Yosry Ahmed suggested,
to handle cases like zswap where the callback has already decremented the
count. However, the incorrect lru->node[nid].nr_items value in zswap is only
an accounting issue: I could not find any code that reads this counter for
zswap. Changing a generic interface to fix an accounting error with no
apparent functional impact did not seem worthwhile.

The third approach is the one implemented in this patch. It keeps the changes
within zswap and fixes the accounting issue, so I think it is appropriate.
